---
title: MCP Console Python
description: >-
  Python clients and framework adapters for persistent R, Python, and SQL
  sessions.
---

The `mcp_console` package connects Python applications to a persistent Console session.
Use `MCPConsole` for synchronous code or `AsyncMCPConsole` for async code.
The application owns its model clients, agents, chats, and tool loops.

```python
from mcp_console import MCPConsole

with MCPConsole() as console:
    print(console.send(python="answer = 42; answer"))
    print(console.send(sql="SELECT 6 * 7 AS answer"))
```

Install the extra for your integration: `client`, `chatlas`, `openai`, `openai-agents`, `anthropic`, or `codex`.
See the [Python integration guide](https://t-kalinowski.github.io/mcp-console/PYTHON.html) for installation and complete examples.

The [API reference](reference/index.qmd) covers connection lifecycle, calls, dependency declarations, and framework adapters.
Both clients accept the same call arguments; `AsyncMCPConsole.send` documents those arguments.
Clients and adapters use the connected server's `send` schema.
Reconnect starts a new session; recreate adapters after reconnecting.
